name: Opposite-side castling race (White long, Black short)

plans.label: Storm the h-file
plans.description: Race the h-pawn at the black king's cover: the storm's whole purpose is an open file for the heavy pieces, with a piece sacrifice on the way when it buys tempi.

success.note: A file has opened at the black king: the h-file is open or half-open for White.

plans.label: Tuck the king to b1
plans.description: The race is counted in tempi, but the king tuck is a tempo the attack repays: the king stands on b1 rather than c1.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Spend the prophylactic tempo', whose success was whether the defensive move blunted the storm. It is now the one move the plan names as its example: the king has tucked to b1. Whether that tempo repaid itself is exactly the judgment the census cannot make. Original success note: 'Whether one defensive tempo blunted the storm is a judgment, not a position property.'

plans.label: Open a queenside file
plans.description: Run the a- and b-pawns at the white king, or give the exchange on the c3 knight, to open an attacking file before the kingside storm lands.

success.note: A file has opened at the white king: the a- or b-file is open or half-open for Black.

plans.label: Open a central file
plans.description: The central break trades the attack's cover open and makes every storm tempo cost something in the middle of the board: the d- or e-file ends up fully open.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Brake in the centre', whose success was whether the central trade defused the storm. It is now the trade itself: a central file has been opened. Original success note: 'Whether a central trade defused the storm is not a pawn shape.'

watch: The tempo count: every non-forcing move hands the other attack a free one.
Pawn moves in front of your own king - each is a hook the enemy storm will use.
Which storm opens lines with pawns alone and which needs a sacrifice to break through.
typicalMistakes: Answering a wing storm with a slower wing storm instead of counting the tempi.
Grabbing material in the middle of the race.
Advancing a defending pawn and handing the storm its hook.

sources: UNGROUNDED: agent-authored strategic claims with no citation, engine evaluation, corpus frequency, or owner review; opposite-castling doctrine rendered from model knowledge.

Trigger narrowing: king placement via pieceOnSquare is a proxy for castling - the vocabulary cannot see castling rights or history, so kings that walked to these squares also fire and kings on a1, f1, or f8 do not. Only the White-long against Black-short orientation is encoded (Dragon and English Attack shape); the mirrored orientation would reverse every plan's side and file targets and remains unauthored. The storm-file signatures can also be satisfied by trades far from the king; they name the opened file, not its cause.
